record_title: Sharp objective-monotonicity frontier for Barzilai–Borwein interval steps
scientific_context: For finite-dimensional real SPD quadratics, every gradient step selected between the contemporaneous BB2 and BB1 steplengths has objective-gap amplification at most (kappa-1)^2. This supremum is sharp even after an exact-line-search warm-up. Consequently kappa<=2 is exactly the condition-number range in which the entire BB interval class is universally objective-monotone; for kappa>2 a two-dimensional construction forces every selector in that interval to increase the objective on the next step.
limitations: Exact arithmetic and finite-dimensional real SPD quadratics only. The claim concerns objective-gap monotonicity and selectors inside the contemporaneous BB2-BB1 interval; it does not cover steps outside that interval, line-search or clipping globalization, other norms, floating-point behavior, asymptotic rates, iteration complexity, or performance. Complete theorem-level text of some broad historical BB treatments, especially the original 1988 article and Fletcher's 2005 chapter, was not inspected in full, leaving residual historical prior-coverage risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy verification of the BB-interval one-step bound, the exact-line-search endpoint construction, selector robustness, and the condition-number frontier.
